title: Design Twitter
description:
Build a small social feed where users post tweets and choose whose tweets to see.

Implement the Twitter class:

  • __init__() creates an empty service.
  • postTweet(userId: int, tweetId: int) -> None publishes a tweet for the user at the current call's time.
  • getNewsFeed(userId: int) -> list[int] returns up to the ten newest tweet IDs authored by the user or users they follow, most recent first.
  • follow(followerId: int, followeeId: int) -> None adds a follow relationship.
  • unfollow(followerId: int, followeeId: int) -> None removes a follow relationship if present.

Users always see their own tweets implicitly, even if they never explicitly follow themselves. Following or unfollowing oneself changes nothing. Repeated follow calls have no extra effect, and unfollowing a user who is not followed is a no-op. Tweet IDs are unique, and recency follows postTweet call order rather than numerical tweet ID.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= userId, followerId, followeeId <= 500.
  • 1 <= tweetId <= 1000000; tweet IDs are unique.
  • At most 30000 calls.

Example 1:

Calls: ["Twitter","postTweet","getNewsFeed","follow","postTweet","getNewsFeed","unfollow","getNewsFeed"]
Arguments: [[],[1,5],[1],[1,2],[2,6],[1],[1,2],[1]]
Output: [null,null,[5],null,null,[6,5],null,[5]]

User 1 initially sees 5, then the newer followed tweet 6, and after unfollowing only 5.

Example 2:

Calls: ["Twitter","follow","postTweet","postTweet","getNewsFeed"]
Arguments: [[],[1,2],[2,3],[1,9],[1]]
Output: [null,null,null,null,[9,3]]

The later local tweet 9 precedes the followed tweet 3.

Example 3:

Calls: ["Twitter","unfollow","follow","follow","postTweet","getNewsFeed"]
Arguments: [[],[1,2],[1,1],[1,2],[1,8],[1]]
Output: [null,null,null,null,null,[8]]

An absent unfollow and self-follow change nothing; the author's own tweet appears once.

An absent unfollow and self-follow change nothing; the author's own tweet appears once.
Unfollowed users do not appear in an empty feed.
Posting order rather than tweet ID determines feed order.
Repeated follow calls do not duplicate a tweet.
Unfollowing removes previously posted followed tweets from the feed.
The author always sees their own post after a self-unfollow.
A followed author's tweet disappears when the relationship is removed.
The feed retains only the ten most recently posted IDs, newest first.
